# The failure taxonomy, regenerated from real failures

**Written:** 2026-09-08.
**Record:** [`results/failure_taxonomy_observed.json`](../results/failure_taxonomy_observed.json), regenerated by `scripts/observe_failures.py`.

`VisibleKind` declares seven ways a failure can be visible without knowing the answer.
Seven categories read as coverage. This note is about what has actually landed in them.

## The taxonomy was computed and thrown away

`judge` has always worked out which kind a visible failure is. `verify/batch.py` stores
it. `agent/trap.py` stores it. `triage/failures.py` exists to sort failures **by cause**.

`sweep/runner.py` did not store it — so the most expensive measurement path in the
project wrote cells that could be counted by outcome and never classified by cause. Every
sweep ever run produced failures whose kind was determined, held in memory for the length
of one function, and dropped before the row was written.

That is this repository's recurring shape, and the same sentence fits prompt caching: the
instrument was built, the number was computed, and the one caller that spends the most
money ignored it. It is fixed — `run_cell` records `visible_kind`, and `summarise_cell`
carries a `visible_kinds` count enumerated over the whole enum.

## What real runs have actually produced

From 48 items, agent role, L0, one-shot and loop, on 2026-09-08:

| kind | observed |
|---|---|
| `shape_mismatch` | 4 |
| `execution_error` | 1 |
| `empty_result` | **never** |
| `null_result` | **never** |
| `timeout` | **never** |
| `no_attempts` | **never** |
| `model_call_failed` | **never** |

`never_observed` is a named field in the record rather than something a reader infers
from five zeros, because that is the part worth arguing about.

**The one kind carrying the failures is the one that was added last.** `shape_mismatch`
went in after the first trap run, when 11 of 35 apparent silent errors turned out to be
the model returning the right numbers beside an extra label column. Before it existed
those were scored as silent errors — the headline metric — inflating it by about a third.
The category with the largest measured effect on the session's own number is the one
nobody predicted.

## Why the five unobserved kinds stay

Deleting a category because it has not fired in 48 items at one level on one role would
be reading the sample for more than it says. Each of the five is reachable, each has a
test that produces it, and three of them describe failures that are *rarer by design*
rather than impossible:

- `model_call_failed` fires when the credential, the account or the rate limiter is the
  problem. It exists precisely because those used to be reported as `execution_error` —
  sending an operator to the SQL and the warehouse when the problem was the key.
- `timeout` needs a query slow enough to hit the ceiling. The warehouse is small.
- `no_attempts` needs a run that made none, which the budget guard can produce.

What would be dishonest is presenting seven categories as seven observed phenomena. The
record says which is which, with the n and the date, so "we have a category for that" and
"we have seen that" stay different sentences.

## This record is provisional and says so

It covers **one role at one level** — a smoke profile run to exercise the machinery, not
a session measurement. Five kinds unobserved across one arm says much less than five
unobserved across the whole matrix, so `covers` is a field in the record rather than a
caveat in prose someone can quote around.

It must be regenerated at the dress rehearsal, when both prompt levels and both scoring
roles run:

```bash
uv run python scripts/observe_failures.py results/sweep --note "<what produced these>"
```

**And it must be regenerated whenever classification changes.** The kind decides which
band an item lands in, the bands are the headline, and a taxonomy record older than the
classifier that produced it is a measurement of a system that no longer exists.
